B5.1.4.1.4 asks learners to use models to explain the result of addition and subtraction of decimals (up to the thousandths); B5.1.4.1.5 asks learners to use models to explain the result of multiplying a decimal (up to the thousandths) by a whole number. The shared modelling representation and identical place-value range are held constant while the operation is extended from additive to multiplicative reasoning, which in these statements is naturally modelled as repeated addition of the same decimal quantity; proficiency in modelling and explaining decimal addition/subtraction therefore supports success in modelling decimal-by-whole-number multiplication. The source code ordering (.4 before .5) is consistent with but not the basis for this judgment. Evidence limitation: both endpoints and the shared standard carry unresolved self/ancestry and merge/audit context, and their source evidence is truncated (32 omitted items each), so placement evidence beyond the statement text and resolved BASIC 5 coordinate is not relied upon; the direction rests on the statement texts alone, hence moderate confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2) under the same Content Standard B6.1.2.1 (mental mathematics strategies and number properties for multiplication/division facts), Sub-Strand 2 Number Operations. B6.1.2.1.1 secures recall/derivation of basic multiplication facts to 81 and related division facts via skip counting, doubling/halving, repeated doubling/halving and 9s/11s patterns; B6.1.2.1.2 applies mental strategies to multiplication more generally, adding annexing-then-adding-zero and the distributive property alongside halving and doubling (LCs 'apply the distributive property for mental multiplication', 'apply the annexing then adding zero strategy'). This is a substantive extension: fluent fact-level mental strategies are the knowledge base decomposed and recombined by distributive and place-value (annexing) strategies for larger products, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second. Same-rank direction rests on this content extension, not on code order or page proximity, which are only weak nomination signals. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement texts and LCs.

The BASIC 5 indicator (rank 1, B5.4.2.1.3) has learners conduct a given probability experiment repeatedly, record the outcomes, and explain the results; the BASIC 6 indicator (rank 2, under B6.4.2.2 on theoretical and experimental probability) requires explaining that experimental probability approaches theoretical probability as the number of trials increases. Shared code prefix, shared Strand/Grade ancestors, and the generic 'compare'/'order' token overlap were treated only as nomination signals, not as the semantic basis.
